# Part IV: Exploring and Sampling {.unnumbered}

Once the data is in shape, look at it before testing it. Chart it, summarise it, and understand its spread and its oddities. A good chart often shows the finding before any test does.

This part covers charts in base R and in ggplot2, factors for categorical data, and descriptive statistics with a profile of a whole ledger. It then turns to probability and to audit sampling, including monetary unit sampling. It ends with the statistical tests that tell whether a difference between offices is real or chance.
